first.rationale: Current onboarding completion and activation declines directly match the historically durable benefits of onboarding simplification. I will verify the original onboarding and pricing records before committing, since competitor pricing creates a plausible alternative but prior evidence flags material retention harm that conflicts with sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying the self-serve onboarding flow. The verified prior result directly addresses both current declines: completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. Pricing is not selected despite the competitive threat because its verified acquisition lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline, conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. Measure qualified activation, completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention by SMB segment before any rollout decision.

final2.rationale: Maintain the simplification experiment. The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-related churn increase urgency, but they do not overturn verified evidence that promotional pricing produced a 12% 30-day retention decline and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the observed completion and activation deterioration and previously improved completion, time-to-value, and retention. The pricing threat remains a material downstream-value risk to monitor, but it is not sufficient evidence to substitute an unsustainable discount experiment for the only slot this cycle.
